analysis:
Examined workflow metadata, the complete patch, and supplied BASE source through line 1068. The only executable change sets DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT=prod in qualify-sdk (HEAD 239–242); build-provider retains the resolved lane environment (BASE 178–182). No supported security regression was identified. Qualification still uses read-only contents permission and reviewed-source checkout; signing still depends on successful build and qualification (BASE 254–258). The supplied signing path retains environment-specific runtime smoke checks (BASE 561, 848), signature/entitlement verification, notarization, exact artifact hashes and publication retention. These controls relate to A-011, A-017, T-013 and T-054; this change does not itself grant serving authorization or alter inference encryption, cache isolation, billing, logout or privileged-helper admission.
Integration question: .github/actions/provider-release-build receives the resolved environment even in the qualification lane (BASE 247–250), while the new job environment explicitly selects prod. Examine that action and provider-swift/Package.swift to establish variable precedence and whether qualification intentionally tests production defaults without substituting production settings into the dev/staging release artifact. Their implementation is outside this supplied scope, so neither a qualification bypass nor complete environment isolation is established. Only indexed threat definitions and selected verbatim details were available; this is not a full PR audit.
